verdict: INTERFACE-SIGN (interface_sign.py): the user's structural idea tested at the resolution real data allows -- use Interactome3D EXPERIMENTAL complexes to call whether two partners of a hub bind SIMULTANEOUSLY (share a PDB -> distinct sites, cooperative) or are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE (structurally resolved but never co-occur -> same site, competitive), then test the DIRECTIONAL prediction on measured perturbation coupling. 1464 cooperative and 969 candidate-competitive KO-partner pairs. mRNA response-correlation: cooperative +0.279 vs competitive +0.115 vs random +0.028. Cooperative pairs ARE more positively coupled than competitive (gap +0.164, 16.0 sigma over label-shuffle) -- but competitive pairs are NOT depleted below the random baseline (comp +0.115 vs random +0.028, p=1.0e+00) -- the competition-specific ANTI-coupling the hypothesis predicts is not detectable. The cooperative>competitive gap that exists is mostly the trivial obligate-complex co-movement (co-crystallised partners co-depend), not a competition signal. READING: structure cleanly separates simultaneous from exclusive binding, and the SIGN idea is biophysically right, but at the whole-cell mRNA readout the competitive (mutual-exclusivity) direction leaves little measurable trace -- consistent with the prior walls (nexus_wall: physical->regulatory two-hop at the random floor; competitive_codep: co-dependency competition null with the topology proxy). The cooperative (obligate-complex) direction is real but largely the trivial co-dependence of co-complex members. HONEST CAVEAT: 'never co-crystallised' conflates true competitors with not-yet-solved pairs; a residue-level interface-overlap call (Interactome3D per-structure interfaces / AF-Multimer) is the ideal the file server would not bulk-serve this session. Deterministic.
